claims.claim: Lassa fever (suspected): Fever >48 hours (5 days) with sore throat and headache; No response to antimalarial treatment; Ondo State is endemic/high-burden for Lassa fever
Bacterial pharyngitis/tonsillitis: Sore throat and headache with fever; Fever persisting beyond typical malaria treatment response
Viral upper respiratory infection: Headache and sore throat are common in viral illnesses; Fever duration of 5 days without localizing signs
Start oral rehydration therapy if the patient is able to drink; monitor hydration status.
Perform a focused examination for Lassa-specific signs (vomiting, diarrhea, bleeding, abdominal pain, hearing loss) and document findings.
If throat exudate or signs of bacterial infection are found, initiate appropriate antibiotic therapy per IMCI guidance (dose to be obtained from verified table).
Instruct the patient to return immediately if any danger sign develops (e.g., bleeding, vomiting everything, convulsions, unconsciousness, severe pallor, dark urine).
